doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: North Texas State and starting jazz studies
summary: At North Texas State he learned mostly from jazz-playing roommates and records, and the students got jazz records played in music appreciation class.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Let me ask you about your experience at North Texas State.

Oh, yeah, right. Well I went there let me see, in 1870 — almost. Wait a minute, 1941 and ‘42 I went there. And it was great. It’s really gotten a lot larger now you know. And it’s a very good school. And I roomed with a bunch of guys, we had a house together, and they were all musicians and all jazz players. So I actually learned more staying there with them, listening to all the records they had. So I learned some from school but we played, we had a drummer, a bassist, pianist, myself and a trumpet and a saxophone. So we played all the time you know, so that was a big help.
With the, what did they have in the school systems at that time in terms of jazz studies?

Well there were no jazz studies at all. We just, we all banded together and in music appreciation we were all good students so they would listen to us. And we asked if we could bring our jazz records in and play them along with the classical records, and they said okay. And with that we were instrumental with starting the jazz part at the school.
